title: Politics and ideologies
description: Review ideology ownership and references before changing project-managed definitions.

rootsHint: Top-level ideologies from the game, a base Mod, an import, or this project.
subtypesHint: Each sub-ideology belongs to one ROOT. Persisted IDs remain stable.
compatibilityHint: These existing rules still expect another government or military naming group. They are reported, not rewritten automatically.
createRootHint: Create a new project-owned ROOT only for a standalone Mod. Imported and base-Mod ROOTs remain source-owned.
rootBodyHint: This is the group definition under common/ideologies. Keep both types and color; add sub-ideologies after creating the group.
createRootBoundary: This creates a new standalone ROOT. It never takes over or rewrites a ROOT owned by the game or another Mod.
createRootStandaloneOnly: A project with a base-Mod dependency uses the ideologies provided by that Mod. Replacing the entire inherited system is not supported here.
createSubtypeHint: Start with the player-facing name, review the suggested ID, then choose its parent ROOT.
scriptIdHint: You may edit this ID before the sub-ideology is saved. After creation it becomes read-only.
createSubtypeBoundary: This adds a project sub-ideology only. It does not take over or rewrite its parent ROOT.
sourceLockRequired: This inherited ideology is not ready for project sub-ideologies yet. Import and lock its exact source before trying again.
deleteAllowed: No references were found. This exact project-managed definition can be deleted with the one-time preview token.
deleteBlocked: Deletion is blocked by these references:
noAutomaticRewrite: No reference will be rewritten, cascaded, or taken over automatically.
visualIdentityHint: Set the political emblem used for each ROOT registered in this project.
visualIdentityBoundary: Only ideologies registered in this project can receive an emblem. Missing emblems keep the game's existing appearance.
iconUploadFailed: Could not save this political emblem: {error}

workbench.projectSourceSummary: Source-owned definitions stay read-only. Project-managed definitions can be created, edited, checked for references, and deleted safely.
workbench.evidenceBoundary: Recognized source and saved status in the program are not game-runtime proof.
workbench.noSearchResults: No ideology or sub-ideology matches this search.
workbench.createHint: Choose what you intend to create first. Creation never changes a country or leader automatically.
workbench.intentSubtypeTitle: Add a sub-ideology to an existing ideology
workbench.intentSubtypeDescription: Create a specific sub-ideology that can later be assigned to a country leader.
workbench.intentRootDescription: Create a complete project-managed ideology that can appear in support and ruling-party controls.
workbench.groupColorHint: This color is used in the political support chart and the in-game ideology's in-game political indicator.
workbench.ruleModeCustom: Paste an ideology definition from an existing Mod
workbench.ruleSourceHint: Keep the default for normal groups. Customize only when carrying over special behavior from an existing Mod.
workbench.advancedScriptHint: This is the group definition written under common/ideologies. You normally do not need to change it; use it to preserve special behavior from an existing Mod.

rootBodyError.missing_types: Keep the types block in the ideology script.
rootBodyError.missing_color: Keep the RGB color block in the ideology script.

workbench.subtypeImpact: Adds this sub-ideology under {root}. It will not change country support, the ruling party, or any leader.
workbench.rootImpact: Creates a new project-managed ideology. It will not change country support, the ruling party, or any leader.
workbench.createdHint: {id} was created. Choose an explicit next step; nothing was assigned automatically.
workbench.followupNeedsContext: Country and leader actions become available when the central workbench supplies its current-country context.
workbench.readOnlyReason: {source} owns this definition. You can inspect it and add project content beneath an eligible ROOT, but cannot edit, delete, take over, or silently overwrite it.
workbench.deleted: Definition deleted after a fresh safety check.
workbench.noReferences: No covered project reference points to this definition.
workbench.selectObject: Select an ideology or sub-ideology to inspect it.
workbench.previewPaneLabel: Political in-game preview and supporting views
workbench.scriptTabHint: Review what this ideology writes under common/ideologies. You normally do not need to change it.
workbench.livePreviewNoDescription: No description in the current content language.
workbench.livePreviewCountryHint: Support and ruling-party values come from the saved opening politics for {tag}; the selected definition updates live before saving.
workbench.livePreviewNoCountryHint: This project has no readable current-country politics yet. The definition preview remains live, but no support value is invented.
workbench.subtypeScriptGeneratedHint: This sub-ideology is injected into the types block of {root} automatically during export.
workbench.sourceScriptReadOnly: This definition belongs to the game, an import, or a base Mod. Its source script remains preserved and read-only.

conflictsBody: **Nothing you already made is affected** — every other ideology, character and country still edits and exports normally. These entries just don't match what the game expects, so they can't be used yet.
conflictsHint: Most come from the early "ideology preset": it stored the game's *groups* in the *sub-ideology* slot. Recreate the entry under the right parent group; removing only clears the invalid record.
conflictReasonDuplicateId: Clashes with the group of the same name — one id cannot be both a group and a sub-ideology
conflictDiscarded: Removed “{id}”. To use it again, create it under the right parent group.
conflictDiscardedWithUse: Removed “{id}”. {count} character(s) were using it — please pick a new ideology for them.
